By reacting an acid with a metal

questions.explanation: Esters are formed by the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst (concentrated sulfuric acid). This is called esterification.

questions.stem: What are esters commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Esters have pleasant, fruity smells and are widely used as flavourings in food, fragrances in perfumes, and as solvents in nail varnish remover and paints.

questions.stem: What is the other product formed alongside an ester during esterification?
questions.explanation: Esterification produces an ester and water: carboxylic acid + alcohol → ester + water. This is a condensation reaction because a small molecule (water) is eliminated.

questions.stem: What ester is formed from ethanoic acid and methanol?
questions.explanation: The ester is named with the alcohol part first (methyl, from methanol) and the acid part second (ethanoate, from ethanoic acid). So ethanoic acid + methanol → methyl ethanoate + water.

questions.stem: What is the functional group present in esters?
questions.explanation: Esters contain the -COO- functional group (ester linkage). This is formed when the -OH from the acid and the H from the alcohol's -OH group are removed as water.

questions.stem: What happens when an ester is hydrolysed with an acid or alkali?

options.text: It breaks down into a carboxylic acid and an alcohol

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of an ester (breaking it down with water, catalysed by acid or alkali) reverses the esterification reaction, producing the original carboxylic acid and alcohol.

questions.stem: Why is concentrated sulfuric acid added during the preparation of an ester?

options.text: It is a reactant that forms part of the ester
It acts as a catalyst to speed up the esterification reaction

questions.explanation: Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst in the esterification reaction. It speeds up the reaction but is not consumed. It also helps remove water, pushing the equilibrium towards products.
